```{r}
#| include: false
source(params$helpers)

m <- readRDS(params$metrics)
gid <- params$id
checks <- rep_checks(m)
group_url <- paste0("https://www.zotero.org/groups/", gid)

# table of items to fix, or a note if the check was not run
fix <- function(items, ...) {
  if (is.null(items)) {
    htmltools::p(htmltools::em("This check was not run."))
  } else {
    rep_fix_table(items, gid, ...)
  }
}

# add the Zotero titles to a table which only has item keys
add_title <- function(items) {
  dplyr::left_join(
    items,
    dplyr::select(m$items, key, Title = title),
    by = "key"
  ) |>
    dplyr::relocate(Title, .after = key)
}

pc <- function(x) if (is.null(x)) NA else paste0(round(x), "%")
```

This report shows the state of the Zotero group **`r params$name`**
([open the group in Zotero](`r group_url`)). It gives an overview of the
literature in the group, and lists the items which should be corrected.

Each item in the lists can be opened in the Zotero **web** library or in
the Zotero **app** on your computer, so that it can be corrected directly.
Corrected items disappear from the lists the next time the report is
updated. Some checks compare the items with
[OpenAlex](https://openalex.org), an open catalogue of scholarly
publications.

## Summary

```{r}
checks |>
  dplyr::transmute(
    Status = rep_status_label(status),
    Check = paste0("[", check, "](#", id, ")"),
    Items = count
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "l", "r"))
```

**Please fix**: these items contain errors. **Please check**: these items
may need a correction. **For information**: no action needed unless the
group uses this, e.g. tags.

## Items to fix

The lists are sorted by importance. Use the search field above a list to
find an item. **web** opens the item in the Zotero web library, **app** in
the Zotero app.

### Retracted publications {#retracted}

These publications have been retracted. Check whether they should still be
cited, and mark or remove them in Zotero.

```{r}
x <- m$openalex_check$met_check_retracted
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) dplyr::transmute(x$items, key, Title = title, DOI = doi),
  doi_cols = "DOI"
)
```

### DOI points to a different publication {#wrong-doi}

The DOI of these items leads to a publication with a different title or
year. Usually the DOI is wrong: open the DOI to see where it leads, and
correct it in Zotero. Differences of one year (e.g. published online before
print) are not listed.

```{r}
x <- m$openalex_check$met_check_mismatch
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(
      x$items,
      key,
      `Title in Zotero` = title_zotero,
      `Year in Zotero` = year_zotero,
      `The DOI leads to` = title_openalex,
      `Its year` = year_openalex,
      DOI = doi
    )
  },
  doi_cols = "DOI"
)
```

### Items which are in the group more than once {#duplicates}

These items are in the group more than once, with the same DOI, or with the
same title, year and first author. Keep one copy and merge or delete the
others, e.g. with *Duplicate Items* in the Zotero app.

```{r}
x <- rep_duplicates(m)
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(x, key = keys, Title = title, Copies = count)
  }
)
```

### DOI field with an invalid DOI {#invalid-doi}

The DOI field of these items contains something which is not a valid DOI.
Correct or remove it.

```{r}
x <- m$identifiers$met_id_doi$zotero$invalid
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    add_title(tibble::tibble(
      key = names(x),
      `Content of the DOI field` = unname(x)
    ))
  }
)
```

### DOI field with a link or prefix instead of the DOI {#doi-form}

The DOI field of these items contains the DOI as a link
(`https://doi.org/…`) or with a prefix (`DOI …`). Citation styles add the
link themselves, so it would appear twice. Replace it with the DOI only.

```{r}
x <- m$identifiers$met_id_doi_form
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(
      x$items,
      key,
      Title = title,
      `Content of the DOI field` = doi_raw,
      DOI = doi
    )
  },
  doi_cols = "DOI"
)
```

### DOI in the wrong field {#misplaced-doi}

These items have no DOI in the DOI field, but a DOI in the URL or Extra
field. Copy the DOI into the DOI field. If the item type has no DOI field,
the DOI is fine in Extra.

```{r}
x <- m$identifiers$met_id_doi_misplaced
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(
      x$items,
      key,
      Title = title,
      `DOI in URL` = doi_in_url,
      `DOI in Extra` = doi_in_extra
    )
  },
  doi_cols = c("DOI in URL", "DOI in Extra")
)
```

### DOI not found in OpenAlex {#not-found}

These DOIs were not found in OpenAlex. The DOI may be wrong: open it to
check. If it leads to the right publication, the publication is simply not
(yet) in OpenAlex and nothing needs to be done.

```{r}
x <- m$openalex_check$met_check_found$zotero_not_in_oa
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) add_title(tibble::tibble(key = names(x), DOI = unname(x))),
  doi_cols = "DOI"
)
```

### Missing or unusual publication year {#year}

These items have no date, a date from which no year could be read, or a year
in the future. Correct the date in Zotero.

```{r}
x <- m$metadata$met_meta_year
problems <- c(
  missing = "No date",
  unparseable = "Year not recognised",
  future = "Year in the future"
)
oa <- m$openalex_check$met_check_date$items
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(
      x$items,
      key,
      Title = title,
      Date = date,
      Problem = unname(problems[problem]),
      `Date in OpenAlex` = if (is.null(oa)) NA_character_ else oa$date[match(key, oa$key)]
    )
  }
)
```

### Empty journal, volume, issue or pages, found in OpenAlex {#fill}

These journal articles have an empty journal, volume, issue or pages field,
and OpenAlex has the value for their DOI. Check it with the DOI and fill in
the field.

```{r}
x <- m$openalex_check$met_check_fill
labels <- c(
  publicationTitle = "Journal",
  volume = "Volume",
  issue = "Issue",
  pages = "Pages"
)
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(
      x$items,
      key,
      Title = title,
      Field = unname(labels[field]),
      `Value in OpenAlex` = value,
      DOI = doi
    )
  },
  doi_cols = "DOI"
)
```

### Language not given as a language code {#language}

The language of these items is not given as a language code (`en`, `fr`,
`en-US`), e.g. as `English` or `eng`. Citation styles only recognise the
codes. Where the language was recognised, the code is shown; otherwise look
up the code in the
[ISO 639-1 list](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_ISO_639_language_codes).

```{r}
x <- m$metadata$met_meta_language
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(
      x$items,
      key,
      Title = title,
      Language = language,
      `Language code` = code
    )
  }
)
```

### Items without DOI, ISBN, ISSN or URL {#no-identifier}

Readers cannot easily find these items. Add a DOI, ISBN, ISSN or URL if one
exists. Some items, e.g. personal communications, have none.

```{r}
x <- m$identifiers$met_id_none
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(x$items, key, Title = title, Type = rep_type(type))
  }
)
```

### Items without DOI, for which OpenAlex has one {#doi-candidates}

OpenAlex was searched by title for items without a DOI (journal articles,
books, book sections, reports, conference papers, theses, preprints). The
publications found are compared by title, year and first author: a *likely*
match agrees in all three, a *possible* match has a similar title, but e.g.
a different year or author. Open the DOI to check that it is the same
publication, and add the DOI in Zotero.

```{r}
x <- m$identifiers$met_id_candidates
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(
      x$items,
      key,
      Title = title,
      Year = year,
      Author = author,
      `Found in OpenAlex` = cand_title,
      `Year (OpenAlex)` = cand_year,
      `Author (OpenAlex)` = cand_author,
      Match = ifelse(is.na(note), match, paste0(match, ": ", note)),
      DOI = doi
    )
  },
  doi_cols = "DOI"
)
```

### Items without tags {#untagged}

These items have no tags. This only matters if the group uses tags, e.g. to
assign items to chapters.

```{r}
x <- m$maintenance$met_maint_tags
fix(
  if (!is.null(x)) {
    dplyr::transmute(x$items, key, Title = title, Type = rep_type(type))
  }
)
```

## The group at a glance

```{r}
oa <- m$profile$met_prof_oa$total
open <- c("gold", "diamond", "green", "hybrid", "bronze")

tibble::tribble(
  ~Figure                                                         , ~Value ,
  "Items in the group"                                            ,
  format(nrow(m$items))                                           ,
  "Items with a valid DOI"                                        ,
  pc(m$identifiers$met_id_doi$zotero$pc)                          ,
  "DOIs found in OpenAlex"                                        ,
  pc(m$openalex_check$met_check_found$pc_in_oa)                   ,
  "Open access, of the publications found in OpenAlex"            ,
  if (is.null(oa)) NA else pc(sum(oa$pc[oa$oa_status %in% open])) ,
  "Grey literature (reports, theses, web pages, preprints, ...)"  ,
  pc(m$profile$met_prof_types$zotero$pc_grey)                     ,
  "Items in English"                                              ,
  pc(m$profile$met_prof_language$zotero$pc_english)               ,
  "Items without language"                                        ,
  pc(m$profile$met_prof_language$zotero$pc_missing)
) |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Value)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = c("l", "r"))
```

### Publication years

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 9
years <- m$profile$met_prof_year$zotero$by_year
if (!is.null(years)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    dplyr::filter(years, !is.na(year)),
    ggplot2::aes(year, count)
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Publication year", y = "Items") +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

### Types of items

```{r}
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-width: 9
types <- m$profile$met_prof_types$zotero$by_type
if (!is.null(types)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    types,
    ggplot2::aes(
      count,
      stats::reorder(rep_type(type), count),
      fill = ifelse(grey, "Grey literature", "Other")
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_col() +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = c("Grey literature" = "#9e9e9e", "Other" = "#2c7fb8")
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Items", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

### Open access

Open access status of the publications found in OpenAlex. *Gold* and
*diamond*: open in an open access journal; *hybrid*: open in a subscription
journal; *green*: an open copy is in a repository; *bronze*: free to read on
the publisher's site; *closed*: not openly available.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 3
#| fig-width: 9
if (!is.null(oa)) {
  ggplot2::ggplot(
    dplyr::filter(oa, !is.na(oa_status)),
    ggplot2::aes(
      count,
      factor(oa_status, levels = rev(c(open, "closed")))
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(fill = "#2c7fb8") +
    ggplot2::labs(x = "Publications", y = NULL) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 13)
}
```

### Most frequent journals

```{r}
journals <- m$profile$met_prof_journals$zotero$top
if (!is.null(journals)) {
  knitr::kable(
    utils::head(journals, 10),
    col.names = c("Journal", "Items"),
    align = c("l", "r")
  )
}
```

### Countries of the authors

Number of publications with at least one author from the country, for the
publications found in OpenAlex.

```{r}
countries <- m$profile$met_prof_countries$by_country
if (!is.null(countries)) {
  utils::head(countries, 15) |>
    dplyr::transmute(
      Country = countrycode::countrycode(
        country,
        "iso2c",
        "country.name",
        warn = FALSE
      ),
      Publications = count
    ) |>
    knitr::kable(align = c("l", "r"))
}
```
